explanation: The Oberwolfach problem for odd n ≥ 3: K_n decomposes into (n−1)/2 copies of any 2-regular F on n vertices, except the two known exceptions C₄+C₅ (n = 9) and C₃+C₃+C₅ (n = 11). The decomposition is encoded as each edge lying in exactly one copy and no extra edges (via the iff). These are exactly the known odd-order exceptions. The statement is faithful and open (known for large n by Glock–Joos–Kim–Kühn–Osthus).
